Psychiatry · published research

Fibromyalgia

Some randomized trials report lower pain or fewer tender points with active PBM, including a trial combining PBM with a static magnetic field. A 2026 meta-analysis found no significant added benefit of PBM plus exercise over exercise alone for pain, function, depression, or quality of life.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Some randomized trials report lower pain or fewer tender points with active PBM, including a trial combining PBM with a static magnetic field. A 2026 meta-analysis found no significant added benefit of PBM plus exercise over exercise alone for pain, function, depression, or quality of life.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Pain > Fibromyalgia category contains 33 titles: 23 human publications, seven reviews or meta-analyses, and three protocols. One additional randomized pilot in fibromyalgia is mapped from the Laser acupuncture category, bringing the relevant publication count to 34. The review papers and protocols overlap completed trials and are not new participant cohorts.

Human and clinical evidence

Results are mixed across populations and treatment types. Ribeiro et al. randomized 90 adults to PBM combined with a static magnetic field or placebo and reported lower pain ratings and fewer tender points in the active group at treatment end and follow-up (2023). A 2026 systematic review found pain reductions in several included trials but could not pool results because the interventions and outcomes differed (Swathi et al. 2026). A separate 2026 meta-analysis found no statistically significant additional improvement in pain, function, depression, or quality of life when PBM was added to exercise; certainty was rated very low by its authors (Macena et al. 2026). The mapped laser-acupuncture pilot is relevant to fibromyalgia but uses a distinct delivery approach (De Lima et al. 2025).

Animal evidence

No animal experiment is listed in the exact fibromyalgia category or the mapped laser-acupuncture record.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone cell, tissue, or ex-vivo fibromyalgia study is listed.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Studies use local laser or LED treatment, whole-body light exposure, high-intensity laser, laser acupuncture, and protocols combined with exercise or a static magnetic field. Wavelength describes the light's color band and can affect tissue penetration. These approaches should not be treated as one dose or one intervention, and the database does not establish an optimal schedule.

Interpretation

A short-term pain benefit is reported in some controlled studies, but the clinical effect is not consistent across protocols. The newer pooled exercise comparison is null, while the broader systematic review finds positive signals but substantial variation. Better powered trials should separate PBM from exercise and other co-interventions.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow-to-moderate for short-term pain reduction with selected PBM protocols in adults with fibromyalgia Very low for added benefit when PBM is combined with exercise or for lasting improvement
Publications and records34 relevant titles (33 exact Pain > Fibromyalgia; 1 mapped Laser acupuncture > Fibromyalgia)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Several controlled studies report lower pain, but they test different lasers, whole-body devices, magnetic fields, and exercise combinations. Recent reviews reach different conclusions and cannot pool all protocols. Larger sham-controlled trials should use common pain and function measures, report dose fully, and follow participants after treatment ends.
